sections.html:
Moon Township lies on the south bank of the Ohio River in western Allegheny County, at an elevation of about 1,175 feet. The 2020 census found 27,261 residents across 24.1 square miles, and the ZIP code is 15108.

Six municipalities touch its borders, and across the river it faces three more:

  • Crescent Township to the north-northwest and the borough of Coraopolis to the north-northeast
  • Hopewell Township in Beaver County to the northwest
  • Findlay Township to the west and southwest, and North Fayette Township to the south
  • Robinson Township to the southeast, east and northeast
  • Edgeworth, Sewickley and Glen Osborne on the opposite bank, linked by the Sewickley Bridge

sections.h2: How did Moon Township get its start?
sections.html:
Moon was created in 1788 as one of the original townships of Allegheny County, and in 1789 it absorbed part of Washington County south of the Ohio River. At that point it covered roughly 145 square miles, and legend says a rider needed two days to cross it. Settlers kept asking for smaller units, so Fayette Township was cut away in 1790, followed by Findlay and Crescent townships. Beaver County later took the land north of the river.

The township stayed rural for almost two centuries. Population was 1,383 in 1850 and still only 2,900 in 1930. Then it jumped to 7,096 in 1950, 10,642 in 1960 and 18,317 in 1970, driven first by defense work and then by the airport.

The Mooncrest housing plan was built in 1943 for defense workers who made armor plate, munitions and ships at the nearby Dravo yard, and its homes were sold to private investors in the mid-1950s. A Cold War missile battery known as Nike Site PI-71 once stood here and is now a nature preserve.

sections.h2: How do the airport and the university shape Moon's housing market?
sections.html:
Pittsburgh International Airport opened in Moon in 1951 and turned the farm country of the western hills into a transportation crossroads, with Parkway West, I-376 and I-79 exits nearby. The passenger terminal later moved to neighboring Findlay Township in 1991, which cost Moon tax revenue, but a large share of the runways and the airport cargo area remain inside the township.

Military and public-sector tenants include the 911th Airlift Wing of the Air Force Reserve Command, the 171st Air Refueling Wing of the Pennsylvania Air National Guard and the National Weather Service office that forecasts for Pittsburgh. Robert Morris University has its main campus here, and the stretch renamed University Boulevard in 2003 is the township's business corridor. Walmart opened a supercenter on the former West Hills Shopping Center site in 2016.

Houses close to University Boulevard or the airport face different noise and traffic conditions than those on quiet interior streets.

sections.h2: What is the weather like, and how does it affect a Moon house?
sections.html:
NOAA normals for 1991 to 2020 put Moon's average January high at 35.6 degrees and low at 19.4, against 83.0 and 62.2 in July. Precipitation totals 41.80 inches a year, between 2.6 and 4.4 inches in every month.

Winter temperatures hover around the freezing line and moisture arrives in every season. Features worth checking before you list include:

  • Roof condition and gutters, since water has to move off a hillside lot
  • Basement dampness and sump pump history
  • Retaining walls, steps and driveway surfaces that heave in winter
  • Furnace age and the efficiency of the heating system

Receipts for roof or drainage work give a hillside seller something concrete to show.

sections.h2: Does Moon Township regulate rental properties and historic homes?
sections.html:
Yes on both counts. Moon requires a rental inspection before each change of occupants. The township's rental packet asks for an inspection request form, an affidavit, an inspection agreement and a rental registration, with a $20 fee per unit. The Fire Marshal's office then schedules the appointment, and owners must report the names of all occupants within 30 days of move-in. An investor buying to rent would go through the same steps.

The Mooncrest Historic District adds another layer. A property there needs a Certificate of Appropriateness before the township will issue a building permit, and the township's Mooncrest Historic Overlay Advisory Committee advises the Board of Supervisors on those certificates. Building permits are required for alterations, additions, porch roofs and sheds, and rules cover windows and doors along building fronts, dryer vents, coal chutes and roofing materials. Ask the township office at 412-262-1700 whether an address falls inside the district.

sections.h2: How much is the transfer tax on a Moon sale?
sections.html:
Moon's county-listed rates are one-half percent for the township and one-half percent for the Moon Area School District, so with the state's 1 percent a sale carries 2 percent in transfer tax. It is paid at recording by its own check, apart from recording fees.

As a worked case, a $300,000 sale in Moon produces $6,000, split $3,000 to the state and $1,500 each to the township and the school district. Allegheny County's own example, a $40,000 house in Shaler Township, is taxed $800 at the same 2 percent. Family transfers can be exempt, and deeds that show no price need a Statement of Value.

An owner who disputes an assessment can go to the county's BPAAR board, whose hearings are held by phone.

sections.h2: What are the options for a quick sale in Moon Township?
sections.html:
Speed comes down to inspection readiness and whether the buyer needs a lender. Moon owners usually compare three routes:

  • List on the open market and wait for a buyer who will live there, the route that can bring the top price for a house in good shape.
  • Sell as is to a cash buyer, a fit for estates, tenant-occupied houses and properties needing repairs.
  • Sell to a neighbor, a relative or an investor you already know.

A house in the Mooncrest district or with a rental history should come with its permits and inspection records, since buyers will ask.

faqs.q: Is Moon Township the same as Moon, Pennsylvania?
faqs.a: Yes. Moon Township is in Allegheny County and is the place most people mean. A separate Moon Township exists in Beaver County, so confirm the county when you search property records.

faqs.q: What is the transfer tax on a house sale in Moon Township?
faqs.a: Two percent altogether: 1 percent to the state, one-half percent to Moon Township and one-half percent to the Moon Area School District.

faqs.q: Do I need a rental inspection to sell a Moon house with a tenant?
faqs.a: Moon inspects a rental before each new occupant, charging $20 a unit, and wants a rental registration within 30 days of move-in. A buyer keeping the tenant should check that the paperwork is on file.

faqs.q: What is the Mooncrest Historic District?
faqs.a: It is a historic overlay area built in 1943 as defense worker housing. A Certificate of Appropriateness must come before any building permit there, with an advisory committee making recommendations to the supervisors.

faqs.q: Which school district serves Moon Township?
faqs.a: The Moon Area School District appears in the Allegheny County transfer tax table for Moon Township. Crescent Township also sits in that district, which helps when comparing nearby addresses.
